Fact.Name: PA-40 line 1a gross compensation
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 10, LINE 1a: "The amount your employer reports in Box 16 of your Form W-2 usually shows your PA-taxable compensation if the W-2 includes PA withholding in Box 17." 72 P.S. §7303(a) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/)(1) Compensation. Sum of W-2 box 16 (all W-2s are PA: a different-state W-2 knocks out via /flowKnockoutBox15IncomeFromDifferentState). #80 part-year: per-W-2 /formW2s/*/paCompensation (PA W-2: box 16; FL W-2: the filer's PA-residency-period allocation).

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 1b unreimbursed employee business expenses
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40.pdf line 1b ("Unreimbursed Employee Business Expenses"). #102: not modeled, so $0; anyone claiming it is knocked out by /flowKnockoutPaUnreimbursedEmployeeExpenses. PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 27, PA SCHEDULE UE (LINE 1b): "Allowable employee business expenses for PA purposes are similar to, but not the same as, expenses for federal purposes. PA law only permits expenses required to perform the duties of a job or profession." Schedule UE is filed per employer (p. 27: "PA Schedule UE – separate schedule for each employer or job") with Sections IV-VII for office, moving, education and depreciation and Schedule NRH allocation (p. 29), which is too much to model here. Line 1b reduces class (1) compensation, 72 P.S. §7303(a)(1) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 1c net compensation
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40.pdf line 1c: "Net Compensation. Subtract Line 1b from Line 1a."

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 2 interest income
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 14, LINE 2: "Report all PA-taxable interest income received or credited during the year." and "Interest income from direct obligations of the U.S. government, the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, and political subdivisions of Pennsylvania is tax exempt." Federal taxable interest minus 1099-INT box 3 (U.S. Savings Bonds and Treasury obligations). Box 8 tax-exempt interest knocks out (PA vs other-state munis not distinguished). 72 P.S. §7303(a) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/)(6). #80 part-year: only the PA-residency-period interest (see /paInterestFullYear).

Fact.Name: PA-taxable interest for the whole year
Fact.Description: #78 line 2 rule for the whole year: federal taxable interest minus 1099-INT box 3. #80: a part-year resident reports only the PA-residency-period part (/paPartYearResidentInterest, capped at this amount); PA-40 IN (2025) p. 43, nonresidents "do not pay PA income tax on ordinary interest".

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 3 dividends
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 15, LINE 3: "Report all dividend income received or credited during 2025." 72 P.S. §7303(a) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/)(5). #86: PA Schedule B line 1 (p. 32): "Enter the amount of dividend income you reported on Line 3b of your federal Form 1040." (income /ordinaryDividends, Form 1099-DIV box 1a). p. 32: if there are no amounts for Lines 2 through 10 of PA Schedule B, "you must report your income on Line 3 of the PA-40, but you do not have to submit PA Schedule B." The adjustments that can arise from a supported 1099-DIV all stop the return instead: line 3 exempt U.S./PA obligation dividends and line 4 nonresident-period dividends (/flowKnockoutPaDividends), line 7 exempt-interest dividends (box 12 is Form 1040 line 2a, interest /taxExemptInterest, and stops a PA-40 on /flowKnockoutPaUnsupportedIncome and /flowKnockoutPaScheduleA) and line 10 capital gains distributions, which p. 32 makes "taxable as dividend income on Line 3" (box 2a, /flowKnockoutPaDividends). Return-of-capital (box 3) is not in box 1a; p. 32: PA-taxable dividend income does not include "Distributions designated as return of capital ... that reduce the basis of your stock". #135 part-year: p. 43, a nonresident does not pay PA income tax on ordinary dividends, so line 3 is only the PA-residency-period part (/paPartYearResidentDividends, capped at the federal amount). 1099-DIVs carry no dates, so the filer allocates. Unanswered, line 3 stays incomplete (not $0). A positive nonresident portion is PA Schedule B line 4 and stops the return.

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 4 net business income
Fact.Description: Tax Reform Code of 1971 §303(a)(2), 72 P.S. §7303(a) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/)(2): "Net profits. The net income from the operation of a business, profession, or other activity, after provision for all costs and expenses incurred in the conduct thereof… but without deduction of taxes based on income." PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 17, LINE 4: "CAUTION: You must use PA Schedule C to report income and expenses from a business or profession… Do not use federal Schedules C or F." PA-40 C (EX) 03-26, https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/pa-40c.pdf line 39 net profit = line 5 − line 38; instructions: "Do not report self-employment taxes to Pennsylvania"; "PA law does not have material participation rules"; federal/PA differences include "meals, travel, and entertainment expense deduction of 100 percent by Pennsylvania"; "Do not report or deduct any transactions related to tax shelters." For a full-year PA resident (/stateReturnIsPa) with only federally supported Schedule C businesses, line 4 is the sum of federal Schedule C line 31 (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/netProfitOrLoss) plus the PA 100% meals add-back (/scheduleCBusinesses/*/paMealsAddBack: writableMeals − line24bDeductibleMeals when mealsAreStandardHalfLimit). A loss within the class is allowed (line 4 may be negative); line 9 already uses GreaterOf 0. A PA/FL part-year resident with any Schedule C, a joint return with any Schedule C loss (IN p. 7: do not net spouses), a yes to the PA tax-shelter screener (/paHasScheduleCTaxShelter; PA-40 C Form 8271 / "Do not report or deduct any transactions related to tax shelters"), farm/Schedule F, or anything still out of scope on federal Schedule C leaves this line incomplete (/flowKnockoutPaUnsupportedIncome or the federal Schedule C/SE stops). Simple Part III inventory/COGS flows through federal line 31 after #277. This slice does not produce a PA Schedule C PDF (/flowKnockoutPaScheduleC); the federal Schedule C PDF is not the PA schedule. $0 when there is no Schedule C, and on a return that is not a PA-40.

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 5 net gain or loss from property
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 17, LINE 5: "Report your gain (loss) from the sale, exchange, or disposition of any kind of intangible property and any real or tangible property." and "PA law does not distinguish between long-term and short term gains (losses)". Sum of Form 8949 column (h); no federal $3,000 loss limit or carryover. May be negative (a net loss) — line 9 then ignores it. #80 part-year: only sales dated in the PA residency period (/form8949Transactions/*/paGainOrLoss); PA-40 IN (2025) p. 43, nonresidents do not pay PA tax on "any gain you realize on the sale, exchange, or disposition of intangible personal property, such as stocks and bonds. You cannot use the loss from such sales against other taxable gains." 72 P.S. §7303(a) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/)(3).

Fact.Name: PA-40 line 6 rents, royalties, patents, copyrights
Fact.Description: Tax Reform Code of 1971 §303(a)(4), 72 P.S. §7303(a) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/)(4): "Net gains or income derived from or in the form of rents, royalties, patents and copyrights." PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 18, LINE 6: "Report the total income (loss) from all PA Schedules E and all PA Schedules RK-1 or NRK-1. Generally, you must use PA Schedule E. You may use federal Schedule E, if using only Part I, and with the following adjustments:" "Report passive rental/royalty loss in full, rather than carry it over to future years." "Add any capital gains and distributions that you report on other federal schedules." "Do not take any depreciation expense on sales tax that you elected to currently expense for PA personal income tax purposes." "You must separately show your share of any rental or royalty gain (loss) that you realize as a partner, a shareholder of a PA S corporation, or other entity." For a full-year PA resident with no Schedule K-1 (/scheduleEHasPartIIIncome false), line 6 is federal Schedule E Part I net income (/scheduleENetIncome: line 3 rents plus line 4 royalties the Part I path already collects, minus expenses). The supported Part I path has no loss, no depreciation, and no property sale in this class, so those adjustments do not change the federal net. A K-1, or Schedule E Part I income of a PA/FL part-year resident, leaves this line incomplete (/flowKnockoutPaUnsupportedIncome). $0 when there is no Schedule E Part I income, and on a return that is not a PA-40.

PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 9: "In computing compensation, only certain expenses are deductible; see the PA Schedule UE instructions beginning on Page 27." p. 29, line 16: "complete Side 1 and include your allowable unreimbursed employee business expenses on Line 1b of your PA-40."

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA-40 line 1b (PA Schedule UE)
Fact.Description: #102: yes to /paHasUnreimbursedEmployeeExpenses. Line 1b needs PA Schedule UE (PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 27: "PA law only permits expenses required to perform the duties of a job or profession."), which this tool doesn't compute; knocked out rather than using $0. An unanswered /paHasUnreimbursedEmployeeExpenses on a PA-40 stays incomplete, so PrintRefusingKnockouts refuses the PDF instead of printing line 1b blank. A non-PA return is complete and false. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(1) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: Ask about PA-exempt obligation dividends
Fact.Description: #86: a PA-40 is filed and there are ordinary dividends (Form 1099-DIV box 1a).

Fact.Name: Has dividends from U.S. or PA obligations
Fact.Description: #86: PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 32, PA Schedule B line 3: "Enter the total amount of any tax-exempt dividends from direct obligations of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, direct obligations of political subdivisions of Pennsylvania and/or direct obligations of the U.S. Government (U.S. Treasury Bonds, Notes, Bills, Certificates, and Savings Bonds) included in any tax-exempt fund or money market fund dividends." and PA-taxable dividend income does not include "Dividends from PA tax-exempt obligations."

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA Schedule B adjustments to dividends
Fact.Description: #86: PA-40 line 3 is federal Form 1040 line 3b only when PA Schedule B lines 2-10 are all $0 (PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 32). Stops the return, rather than overstating line 3, when there are dividends and (1) yes to /paHasExemptObligationDividends (PA Schedule B line 3, p. 32; the exempt part would also go on Schedule SP line 2), or (2) a PA/FL part-year resident whose ordinary dividends received while not a PA resident (/paPartYearNonresidentDividends) are greater than $0: p. 43, "As a nonresident, you do not pay PA income tax on ordinary interest, ordinary dividends", so that nonresident-period part is a PA Schedule B line 4 adjustment (p. 32: "dividend income for a part-year resident taxpayer during the period the taxpayer was a nonresident") and Schedule SP line 6 non-PA income (p. 38). 1099-DIVs carry no dates; the filer allocates (/paPartYearResidentDividends). When that amount equals the federal total, line 4 is $0 and this clause is false. Unanswered, the nonresident amount stays incomplete, so this clause and /paLine3 stay incomplete (not $0). An unanswered /paHasExemptObligationDividends on a return with dividends stays incomplete the same way; or (3) #86b: any Form 1099-DIV box 2a capital gain distributions. p. 32: "Capital gains distributions are taxable as dividend income on Line 3. Do not report capital gains distributions on PA Schedule D." PA Schedule B line 10: "Enter the amount of capital gains distributions included as capital gains on federal Schedule D. If federal Schedule D is not required, enter the amount of capital gains distributions reported directly on Schedule 1 of the federal return." A line 10 amount requires submitting PA Schedule B, which is not supported. PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(5) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: income PA-40 core does not classify
Fact.Description: #78: PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 17 (LINE 4: full-year federally supported Schedule C is /paLine4; a PA/FL part-year resident with any Schedule C still stops — p. 43 has no business allocation; a joint return with any Schedule C loss stops — p. 7: "You may not offset the income of the taxpayer with a loss from the spouse and vice versa"; a yes to /paHasScheduleCTaxShelter stops — PA-40 C Form 8271 / "Do not report or deduct any transactions related to tax shelters"; farm/Schedule F and federal Schedule C out-of-scope lines stay stopped elsewhere; PA Schedule C is required and not produced — /flowKnockoutPaScheduleC), p. 18 (LINE 6: full-year federal Schedule E Part I is /paLine6; a K-1 or a PA/FL part-year resident with Schedule E Part I still stops), pp. 13-14 (1099-R: PA taxability depends on plan/age/code), 1099-MISC (must be classified), Form 1040 line 2a tax-exempt interest from 1099-INT box 8 and 1099-DIV box 12 exempt-interest dividends (PA taxes other states' obligations, exempts PA ones: p. 14), W-2 with wages but no box 16 PA wages, and joint returns with property sales (p. 7, not modeled). PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled (full-year or PA/FL part-year PA-40), so returns with no PA-40 are not stopped by it or shown its screen. 1099-INT box 2 early withdrawal penalty (interest /earlyWithdrawalPenaltyTotal greater than $0): PA-40 IN (2025) p. 15, LINE 2, Forfeited Interest Penalty: "You may offset the penalty for premature redemption or withdrawal of a time savings account or certificate of deposit, only against the interest income you received in the same taxable year from that account or certificate. You cannot offset this penalty against other interest income. If your total penalty exceeds the related interest income, you may report the excess as a loss on PA Schedule D." The account-level interest is not collected (one 1099-INT can cover several accounts) and PA Schedule D for the excess is not modeled, so the PA-40 line 2 offset cannot be computed.

Fact.Name: PA-taxable interest above which this tool stops (PA Schedule A)
Fact.Description: #123: $2,500, a limit this tool sets on top of the booklet's PA Schedule A triggers (/flowKnockoutPaScheduleA).

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA Schedule A (interest) is required and not produced
Fact.Description: #123: PA Schedule A is required and this tool doesn't produce it. PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 14, LINE 2: "See the instructions beginning on Page 31 for when to complete and submit PA Schedule A." p. 31, PA SCHEDULE A (LINE 2): "If your total PA-taxable interest income (taxpayer, spouse, and/or joint) is equal to the amount reported on your federal return and you have no amounts for Lines 2 through 15 (not including subtotal Lines 4 and 10) of PA Schedule A, you must report your income on Line 2 of the PA-40, but you do not have to submit PA Schedule A. If there are any amounts (taxpayer, spouse and/or joint) for any of the Lines 2 through 15 (not including subtotal Lines 4 and 10) of PA Schedule A, you must complete and submit PA Schedule A with your PA-40." The same rule is in the PA Schedule A (2025) instructions (https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40a.pdf). Cases, from the information this tool collects: (1) 1099-INT box 3 interest on U.S. obligations, which PA exempts (p. 14) and Schedule A takes out on line 7 ("Interest income from direct obligations of the U.S. government"); (2) 1099-INT box 8 tax-exempt interest, Schedule A line 2 ("Tax-exempt interest income included in Line 2a of your federal return"; also /flowKnockoutPaUnsupportedIncome); (3) a PA/FL part-year resident with PA-taxable interest, whose PA interest (PA residency period only, /paLine2) is not "equal to the amount reported on your federal return"; (4) PA-taxable interest (/paLine2) over /paScheduleAThreshold ($2,500), a limit this tool sets; the booklet ties the requirement to the cases above, not to a dollar amount. Other Schedule A lines (K-1 interest, annuities and life insurance, charitable gift annuities, 529 and MSA/HSA distributions, PA S corporation and partnership interest) come from income that already stops the PA return or that this tool doesn't collect. The box 2 early withdrawal penalty is /flowKnockoutPaUnsupportedIncome. PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(6) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: PA-taxable dividends above which this tool stops (PA Schedule B)
Fact.Description: #123: $2,500, a limit this tool sets on top of the booklet's PA Schedule B triggers (/flowKnockoutPaScheduleB).

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA Schedule B (dividends) is required and not produced
Fact.Description: #123, #154: PA Schedule B is required and this tool doesn't produce it. PA-40 Schedule B (2025) form and instructions https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40b.pdf (SHA-256 c6d8f5cdd63045e1e40b6deeced2c80b23006b7700befe3b8f0c430f2b40a0d4), PDF p. 3, WHO MUST COMPLETE: "PA resident and part-year resident taxpayers must complete and include PA-40 Schedule B with an originally filed PA-40, Personal Income Tax Return, if there are any amounts on Lines 2 through 11 (not including subtotal Line 6)." PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 15, LINE 3: "See instructions for this schedule beginning on Page 32 for when to complete and submit PA schedule B." p. 32 says the same for Lines 2 through 10. Cases, from the Form 1099-DIV facts (dividends module) and the PA questions: (1) Line 3 (PDF p. 4, LINE 3: "Enter the total amount of any tax-exempt dividends from direct obligations of the Commonwealth of Pennsylvania, direct obligations of political subdivisions of Pennsylvania, and/or direct obligations of the U.S. Government"): yes to /paHasExemptObligationDividends with dividends. (2) Line 4 (PDF p. 4, LINE 4: "Examples would include, but are not limited to: dividend income for a part-year resident taxpayer during the period the taxpayer was a nonresident; nominee capital gains distributions"): ordinary dividends received while not a PA resident (/paPartYearNonresidentDividends greater than $0) on a PA/FL part-year return. 1099-DIVs carry no dates, so the filer allocates (/paPartYearResidentDividends). When every ordinary dividend was received while a PA resident, line 4 is $0 and this clause is false (PA-40 line 3 is the federal amount; Schedule B is not required for the move). Unanswered, the nonresident amount stays incomplete, so this clause and /paLine3 stay incomplete (not $0). An unanswered /paHasExemptObligationDividends on a return with dividends stays incomplete the same way. Also any 1099-DIV received as a nominee (dividends /flowKnockoutDividendNominee, which also stops the federal return). (3) Line 10 (PDF p. 4, LINE 10: "Enter the amount of capital gains distributions included as capital gains on federal Schedule D. If federal Schedule D is not required, enter the amount of capital gains distributions reported directly on the federal return."): any Form 1099-DIV box 2a amount (/totalCapitalGainDistributions greater than $0). (4) PA-taxable dividends (/paLine3: federal Form 1040 line 3b for a full-year resident, or the PA-residency-period part for a part-year resident) over /paScheduleBThreshold ($2,500), a limit this tool sets; the booklet ties the requirement to the cases above, not to a dollar amount. Line 7 (PDF p. 4, LINE 7: "exempt-interest dividends reported in Box 12 of federal Form 1099-DIV") is Form 1040 line 2a (interest /taxExemptInterest) and stops a PA-40 on /flowKnockoutPaUnsupportedIncome and /flowKnockoutPaScheduleA. Lines 2, 8, 9 and 11 (Schedule K-1 and PA RK-1 dividends, Section 965 repatriation, other additions) come from 1099-DIV boxes or income that already stop the return (dividends /flowKnockoutDividendUnsupportedBoxes, which no longer includes box 12) or that this tool doesn't collect. /flowKnockoutPaDividends stops the same Line 3, Line 4 part-year and Line 10 cases with its own explanation; this fact is the single Schedule B test. PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(5) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA Schedule D (sale of property) is required and not produced
Fact.Description: #123: any sale, exchange or disposition of property reported for PA, gain or loss. PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 17, LINE 5: "Report your gain (loss) from the sale, exchange, or disposition of any kind of intangible property and any real or tangible property." and "Report your total net gains (losses) on PA Schedule D." p. 33, PA SCHEDULE D (LINE 5): "The Schedule D line-by-line instructions are on the schedule." PA Schedule D (2025) instructions (https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40d.pdf), WHO MUST COMPLETE: "PA-40 Schedule D must be completed and included with an originally filed PA-40 if there are any transactions involving the sale, exchange, or disposition of property. PA-40 Schedule D must be completed even if the only transaction is to report a loss." This tool doesn't produce PA Schedule D. Stops when PA-40 line 5 (/paLine5) is not $0, or when there is any Form 8949 sale that PA counts: every sale for a full-year resident, and sales in the PA residency period (/form8949Transactions/*/paSoldWhilePaResident) for a PA/FL part-year resident (p. 43: a nonresident does not pay PA tax on gains from intangible property). PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled. 72 P.S. §7303(a)(3) (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7303/).

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA Schedule C (business) is required and not produced
Fact.Description: PA-40 IN (2025), https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 17, LINE 4: "CAUTION: You must use PA Schedule C to report income and expenses from a business or profession… Do not use federal Schedules C or F." This tool does not produce a PA Schedule C PDF; the federal Schedule C PDF is not the PA schedule. Stops when a PA-40 is filed (/stateReturnPaFiled) and there is Schedule C income (/hasScheduleCBusinesses). Wired into /flowIsKnockedOut via /flowKnockoutStateReturn and into PrintRefusingKnockouts.FACT_PATHS so the PA Schedule C attachment print-refuses. Full-year federally supported Schedule C still figures /paLine4. Tax Reform Code of 1971 §303(a)(2), 72 P.S. §7303(a)(2).

Fact.Name: PA school district code where the filer lived on Dec. 31
Fact.Description: #123: PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 5, School Code and School District Name: "You must enter the five-digit code and name of the school district where you lived on Dec. 31, 2025, even if you moved after Dec. 31, 2025." Allowed values are the 500 five-digit codes in "PA SCHOOL DISTRICTS & CODES BY COUNTY", pp. 46-47 (a district that spans counties is listed under each with the same code). 99999 is not accepted here: p. 6 reserves it for "Nonresidents or part-year residents who did not reside in the state as of Dec. 31, 2025", which /paSchoolCode fills in for a PA-to-FL mover, who is not asked. A FL-to-PA mover is asked: p. 6, "Part-year residents who resided in Pennsylvania as of Dec. 31, 2025, should enter the school district code of the physical address of their domicile or principal residence."

Fact.Name: PA-40 school code for a filer who did not live in PA on Dec. 31
Fact.Description: #123: PA-40 IN (2025) p. 6: "Nonresidents or part-year residents who did not reside in the state as of Dec. 31, 2025, should enter 99999 in the school district code field."

Fact.Name: PA-40 filer did not live in PA on Dec. 31
Fact.Description: #123/#80: a supported PA/FL part-year resident who moved from PA to FL.

Fact.Name: Ask for the PA school district code
Fact.Description: #123: a PA-40 is filed and the filer lived in PA on Dec. 31 (full-year resident, or FL-to-PA mover).

Fact.Name: PA-40 School Code
Fact.Description: #123: PA-40 (2025) "School Code" box. 99999 for a PA-to-FL mover (p. 6); otherwise the code the filer entered (/paSchoolDistrictCode, p. 5).

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 1 PA taxable income
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, Section III: "1. PA Taxable Income. Enter your total PA Taxable Income amount from Line 9 of your PA-40 form."

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 2 nontaxable interest, dividends, gains
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, line 2: "Include the tax-exempt interest … as well as any exempt gains from investments in direct obligations of the federal government, Pennsylvania, and political subdivisions of Pennsylvania." Supported source: 1099-INT box 3 (U.S. obligation interest excluded from PA-40 line 2). Box 8 tax-exempt interest already knocks out (#78).

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 6: interest received while living outside PA
Fact.Description: #107: PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, line 6: "6. Non-PA income. Part-year residents and nonresidents must complete this line. Enter the total of all income, not already reported on this schedule, that you (and your spouse, if applicable) earned, received or realized while residing outside Pennsylvania." A part-year resident's PA-taxable interest for the year (/paInterestFullYear) minus the PA-period interest on PA-40 line 2 (/paLine2, capped at the year's amount, so never below $0). p. 43: "As a nonresident, you do not pay PA income tax on ordinary interest". U.S. obligation interest is already on Schedule SP line 2 for the whole year. Full-year residents: $0.

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 6: net gain or loss from sales while living outside PA
Fact.Description: #107: sum of /form8949Transactions/*/paSpNonPaPeriodGainOrLoss. PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 17, LINE 5: "Report your gain (loss) from the sale, exchange, or disposition of any kind of intangible property and any real or tangible property." Sales net within the class. A net loss is not added to line 6 and stops the return when forgiveness is possible (/flowKnockoutPaSpUnsupported case 6): line 6 asks for "the total of all income" and the booklet doesn't say whether a non-PA-period loss reduces it.

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 6 Non-PA income
Fact.Description: #107: PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, line 6: "6. Non-PA income. Part-year residents and nonresidents must complete this line. Enter the total of all income, not already reported on this schedule, that you (and your spouse, if applicable) earned, received or realized while residing outside Pennsylvania." p. 37, "Nonresidents and Part-Year Residents": "Such taxpayers must include in their eligibility income all income as described whether earned within or outside Pennsylvania." Part-year (PA/FL) residents: compensation earned while living in FL (/formW2s/*/paSpNonPaPeriodCompensation) + FL-period interest (/paSpNonPaPeriodInterest) + FL-period net gain from sales (/paSpNonPaPeriodGainOrLoss, if positive). Dividends: a part-year resident with any dividends stops the return (/flowKnockoutPaDividends, #86), and Schedule C, Schedule E, 1099-R, 1099-MISC and 1099-G income already knock out (#101/#105). Full-year residents: $0 (no time outside PA).

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 11 Eligibility Income
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, line 11: "Eligibility Income is the total amount of your PA-taxable and nontaxable income that you use to determine your percentage of Tax Forgiveness." Lines 3–10 (alimony, insurance/inheritances, gifts/awards, non-PA income, nontaxable military, excluded home-sale gain, nontaxable educational assistance, cash support from outside the home) are not collected; a yes to /paHasSpNontaxableIncome knocks out (/flowKnockoutPaSpUnsupported). Line 6 non-PA income (/paSpLine6, #107) is $0 for full-year residents and computed for PA/FL part-year residents. Married: p. 37: "you must determine your total (your Eligibility Income plus your spouse’s Eligibility Income) joint Eligibility Income" — MFJ facts already cover both spouses.

Fact.Name: Schedule SP Section II line 2 dependent children
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 37, Section II: "A dependent is a minor or adult child claimed as a dependent on a 2025 federal income tax return." "child includes the natural child, adopted child, or step-child of a parent. Child also includes a grandchild of a grandparent and a foster child of a foster parent." "You cannot claim any other adult as a dependent". Counts claimed dependents whose relationship is biological/adopted/foster/stepchild or grandchild.

Fact.Name: Schedule SP: highest Eligibility Income for 100% forgiveness
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 39, ELIGIBILITY INCOME TABLE 1 (Unmarried, Separated and Deceased Claimants): YOU "$6,500"; 1 dependent child "$16,000", 2 "$25,500" … 9 "$92,000" (+$9,500 each). TABLE 2 (Married Claimants, even if filing separately): YOU & SPOUSE "$13,000"; 1 child "$22,500" … 9 "$98,500". 72 P.S. §7304 (https://codes.findlaw.com/pa/title-72-ps-taxation-and-fiscal-affairs/pa-st-sect-72-7304/)(a)-(b).

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 15 percentage of Tax Forgiveness
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38, line 15: "Find your percentage using your dependents from Section II, Line 2, and your Eligibility Income from Section III, Line 11, and the appropriate Eligibility Income Table." p. 39 tables: "If your Eligibility Income from PA Schedule SP, Line 11, does not exceed:" the column amount, "Then your Percentage of Tax Forgiveness and the Decimal Equivalent is:" 100% "1.0", 90% ".90" … 10% ".10" in $250 columns (Table 1 YOU: $6,500 … $8,750; Table 2: $13,000 … $15,250). Above the 10% column: 0.

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 14 net PA tax liability
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38: "12. PA Tax Liability. Enter the amount of your tax due from your PA40, Line 12." "13. Less Resident Credit. Enter your credit from your PA-40, Line 22." "14. Net PA Tax Liability. Subtract Line 13 from Line 12." PA-40 line 22 (Schedule G-L) is $0 (knockout).

Fact.Name: Schedule SP line 16 Tax Forgiveness credit
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 38: "16. Tax Forgiveness Credit. Multiply Line 14 by the decimal on Line 15". When an unsupported case applies, /flowKnockoutPaSpUnsupported blocks submission.

Fact.Name: Schedule SP: Eligibility Income so far is within the 10% column
Fact.Description: #79: line 11 can only rise from items not yet collected (lines 3–10), so if lines 1+2 already exceed the 10% column (p. 39) no forgiveness is possible and the unsupported-case checks are moot.

Fact.Name: Has nontaxable income counted for PA Tax Forgiveness
Fact.Description: #79: PA-40 IN (2025) p. 38, Schedule SP Section III lines 2–10 nontaxable income other than U.S. obligation interest: alimony, life insurance or inheritances (1099-R code 4/7), gifts/awards/prizes, nontaxable military pay, excluded home-sale gain, nontaxable scholarships/grants, support or cash from outside the household, nontaxable cafeteria-plan sickness/disability/supplemental unemployment/strike benefits, foster care payments, and unemployment compensation.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA Tax Forgiveness case not supported
Fact.Description: #79: only when /paSpCouldQualify. (1) Separated / married filing separately: PA-40 IN (2025, latest booklet; 2026 not yet published) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 37 "Separated means: • Separated and living apart at all times during the last six months of 2025; or • Separated pursuant to a written separation agreement." (uses Table 1) and "When filing separately, the taxpayer and spouse must combine their eligibility incomes" (spouse data not collected). (2) A filer claimed as a dependent: p. 36 eligible only if "You are not a dependent on another person's federal tax return" and p. 37 a dependent child qualifies only "If that child’s parents qualify for Tax Forgiveness" (parents' data not collected). (3) More than 9 dependent children: p. 39 "If claiming more than nine (9) dependent children, go to the PA Personal Income Tax Guide". (4) Nontaxable Section III income (/paHasSpNontaxableIncome). Unanswered, that clause stays incomplete when /paSpCouldQualify is true, so PrintRefusingKnockouts refuses the PDF instead of printing those lines blank. When /paSpCouldQualify is complete and false the knockout stays complete and false. (5) Any Form 1099-G (unemployment): its Eligibility Income treatment is not modeled. (6) #107 PA/FL part-year resident with a net loss from sales made while living outside PA (/paSpNonPaPeriodGainOrLoss below $0): PA-40 IN (2025) p. 38 line 6 asks for "the total of all income" earned, received or realized while residing outside Pennsylvania, and the booklet doesn't say whether a loss reduces it. Part-year Eligibility Income is otherwise whole-year (p. 37, "Such taxpayers must include in their eligibility income all income as described whether earned within or outside Pennsylvania."; /paSpLine6). PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled.

Fact.Name: PA part-year move options
Fact.Description: #80: the supported moves are between Pennsylvania and Florida. Any other state stops the return.

Fact.Name: Which move the filer made during the year
Fact.Description: #80: asked only when the filer answered "I lived in more than 1 state" (/filerResidenceAndIncomeState = moreThanOne). PA-40 IN (2025) p. 6: "If you moved into Pennsylvania during 2025, fill in this oval even though you were a PA resident at the end of 2025. If you moved from Pennsylvania during 2025, fill in this oval even though you were not a PA resident at the end of 2025."

Fact.Name: Date the filer started living in the new state
Fact.Description: #80: the first day of residence in the new state. Moving PA to FL: PA residency period is Jan. 1 through the day before this date. Moving FL to PA: PA residency period is this date through Dec. 31. PA-40 IN (2025) p. 6 describes a residency period by its "earliest starting date if you moved into Pennsylvania and latest ending date if you moved out of Pennsylvania" (said of spouses electing one residency period for a joint return).

Fact.Name: Ask about a move between PA and FL
Fact.Description: #80: the filer said they lived in more than one state.

Fact.Name: Moved from PA to FL
PA part-year resident whose other state is Florida
Fact.Description: #80: lived in more than one state and the move was PA to FL or FL to PA. A move involving any other state ("other") is not supported and stays knocked out by /flowKnockoutUnsupportedState (filers /hasIncomeInScope).

Fact.Name: PA-40 Residency Status oval (P) Part-Year Resident
Fact.Description: #80: PA-40 IN (2025) p. 6, "(P) Part-Year Resident". True for a supported PA/FL part-year return; false for a full-year (R) resident.

Fact.Name: W-2 box 15 state for a PA part-year resident
Earliest move date that makes a part-year return
Fact.Description: #80: a move on Jan. 1 is a full year in the new state; the date must fall in the tax year.

Fact.Name: Latest move date in the tax year
PA part-year filer has ordinary dividends
Fact.Description: #135: a supported PA/FL part-year resident with ordinary dividends (Form 1099-DIV box 1a, dividends /hasDividendIncome). 1099-DIVs carry no dates, so the filer allocates the PA-residency-period part (/paPartYearResidentDividends). PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 43: "As a nonresident, you do not pay PA income tax on ordinary interest, ordinary dividends, and any gain you realize on the sale, exchange, or disposition of intangible personal property, such as stocks and bonds."

Fact.Name: Ordinary dividends received while a PA resident
Fact.Description: #135: the filer's allocation of Form 1099-DIV box 1a received during the PA residency period. PA-40 IN (2025) p. 43: a nonresident does not pay PA income tax on ordinary dividends. PA-40 Schedule B (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40b.pdf PDF p. 4, LINE 4, lists "dividend income for a part-year resident taxpayer during the period the taxpayer was a nonresident" as a line 4 example. Capped at federal ordinary dividends on /paLine3. PDF p. 3, WHO MUST COMPLETE: Schedule B is required only "if there are any amounts on Lines 2 through 11 (not including subtotal Line 6)." When this amount equals the federal total, that line 4 amount is $0.

Fact.Name: Ordinary dividends received while not a PA resident
Fact.Description: #135: federal ordinary dividends (income /ordinaryDividends, Form 1040 line 3b) minus /paPartYearResidentDividends, not below $0. This is the PA Schedule B line 4 amount for ordinary dividends received while not a PA resident (2025 PA-40 Schedule B, PDF p. 4). The schedule is not produced, so a positive amount stops the return (/flowKnockoutPaScheduleB and /flowKnockoutPaDividends). $0 when every ordinary dividend was received while a PA resident.

Fact.Name: PA part-year filer has PA-taxable interest for the whole year
Interest received while a PA resident
Fact.Description: #80: PA-40 IN (2025) p. 43: "As a nonresident, you do not pay PA income tax on ordinary interest, ordinary dividends, and any gain you realize on the sale, exchange, or disposition of intangible personal property, such as stocks and bonds." So only interest received during the PA residency period is PA-taxable. 1099-INTs carry no dates, so the filer allocates.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA part-year case not supported
Fact.Description: #80. (1) Joint return: PA-40 IN (2025) p. 7, spouses "must file separate returns if: ... 2. Your taxable years begin on different dates for part-year residents; ... 5. One of you is a PA resident and the other is not", and joint part-year filing requires electing the same residency period (p. 6); the spouse's residency isn't collected. (2) Move date outside Jan. 2 - Dec. 31 of the tax year. (3) A W-2 from a state other than PA or FL, or a FL W-2 with box 17 state tax withheld (some other state's tax). PA-only: gated on stateReturn /stateReturnPaFiled.

Fact.Name: PA part-year: pay for work in PA while not a PA resident that is not in a PA W-2's box 16
Fact.Description: #135: PA-40 IN (2025) https://www.pa.gov/content/dam/copapwp-pagov/en/revenue/documents/formsandpublications/formsforindividuals/pit/documents/2025/2025_pa-40in.pdf p. 43, Compensation: "As a nonresident, you pay PA income tax on compensation for services you perform in Pennsylvania. Your PA employer should report and withhold PA tax from the exact amount of your PA-taxable compensation. If your employer does not report, or incorrectly reports, your PA-taxable compensation, you must use PA Schedule NRH to apportion your compensation and any allowable employee business expenses." A FL W-2 only asks for pay earned while a PA resident (/formW2s/*/paPartYearResidentPeriodWages), so pay for work done in PA during the FL period would otherwise be $0 on PA-40 line 1a. Yes stops the return (/flowKnockoutPaNonresidentPaSourcePay) until PA Schedule NRH is supported.

Fact.Name: Flow knockout: PA-source pay in the nonresident period (PA Schedule NRH)
Fact.Description: #135: yes to /paPartYearHasNonresidentPaSourcePay on a PA/FL part-year return. PA-40 IN (2025) p. 43: "If your employer does not report, or incorrectly reports, your PA-taxable compensation, you must use PA Schedule NRH to apportion your compensation". This tool doesn't produce PA Schedule NRH. Complete and false when there is no PA return or it is not a PA/FL part-year return. An unanswered /paPartYearHasNonresidentPaSourcePay on a PA/FL part-year return stays incomplete, so PrintRefusingKnockouts refuses the PDF instead of printing line 1a without that pay. 72 P.S. §7302(b): a nonresident is taxed on "each of the classes of income hereinafter enumerated in section 303 from sources within this Commonwealth". Wired into stateReturn /flowKnockoutStateReturn.
